title: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter

posts.topic_title: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.author: Julian
posts.post_subject: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.content_md: Please can you recommend a suitable light meter for a 25 MW Hene (632nm) laser set up to measure beam ratios at the plate.

posts.topic_title: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.post_subject: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.content_md:
If you find one used or afford one, the best IMO is the Ophir Nova with a PD300. This is a small head with a 1cm X 1 cm detector. It allows you to read watts/cm2 right off the bat without calulating. Hope you have deep pockets 

Good Luck

posts.topic_title: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.post_subject: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.content_md:
A used Ophir Nova just went for $1000 on ebay, so yes you need deep pockets. However I think several people are happy with less expensive options like the Andover HP-1 and the Sper meter. You can also make simple home made meters. See: [http://www.holowiki.org/index.php/Light_Meter](http://www.holowiki.org/index.php/Light_Meter)

 Here is more info on the HP-1: [http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=4429](http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=4429)

posts.topic_title: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.author: JohnFP
posts.post_subject: Can you recommend a HeNe Light Meter
posts.content_md:
Jeff turned me on to LaserCheck, a pocket meter by Coherent. I think it is about $400 brand new. But it is wavelength selectable so you can use it if you decide to change color wavelengths. It also allow you to measure in mW and uW. So you can use it to check raw beam power and power at the plate after expansion. I am very pleased with it.

[http://www.coherent.com/Lasers/index.cf ... 50&loc=830](http://www.coherent.com/Lasers/index.cfm?fuseaction=show.page&ID=250&loc=830)
